claims.text: Additive manufacturing can produce tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys suitable as the starting material.
A single-phase or minimally segregated microstructure is typical of current additive-manufacturing processing for the proposed tungsten-based RHEA.
An optimized post-fabrication annealing treatment can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten refractory HEA.
The annealing treatment will produce a fine, homogeneous distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates throughout the alloy matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracking.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and thereby support a favorable strength-ductility combination.
The coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
The nanoprecipitates promote recombination of irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
The nanoprecipitates limit helium-bubble growth and coalescence during irradiation.
Approximately 200 keV helium irradiation at about 900 °C represents reactor-relevant plasma-facing exposure conditions.
The annealed material will have statistically significantly smaller helium bubbles than the as-fabricated baseline.
The annealed material will have a statistically significantly lower helium-bubble number density than the as-fabricated baseline.
The annealed material will exhibit less irradiation hardening than the as-fabricated baseline.
The annealed material will maintain its yield strength after helium irradiation.
The annealed material will maintain its ductility after helium irradiation.
The unannealed additive-manufactured baseline has acceptable mechanical properties.
The unannealed baseline exhibits more pronounced helium-bubble growth than the proposed annealed material.
The radiation-tolerance benefit depends on obtaining an optimal nanoprecipitate volume fraction.
The proposed benefit may not persist at irradiation temperatures or conditions substantially outside the stated range.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls for lower irradiation hardening, whereas the falsification rule refers to 'improved irradiation hardening,' which literally suggests increased hardening and makes the intended mechanical criterion ambiguous.
